description: 20 Grand Prix strategy scenarios. 'real' scenarios pull the car and field state from the Parquet lakehouse (OpenF1 data) at the decision lap; 'synthetic' scenarios are historical-style traps with an explicit state. Field rows are [code, number, position, gap_to_leader_ms, compound, tyre_age_laps]. Ground truth lists every acceptable call; for real scenarios it is what the team actually did (and what worked), for synthetic ones it follows from the regulations and race situation.

scenarios.title: 2023 Singapore GP, lap 20: safety car with one dry compound used
scenarios.question: Safety car is out. Norris is on 19-lap-old mediums and has only used the medium. Do we box?

ground_truth.historical: Norris (and Sainz, Leclerc) boxed for hards under the lap-20 safety car and ran to the flag; Norris finished P2.

scenarios.title: 2023 Singapore GP, lap 44: VSC for Ocon, Hamilton on old hards
scenarios.question: VSC deployed. Hamilton is P5 on 23-lap-old hards with 18 laps to go. Mediums and softs available.

ground_truth.historical: Mercedes double-stacked for fresh mediums under the VSC; Hamilton climbed to P3.

scenarios.title: 2023 Singapore GP, lap 44: VSC, Sainz leading on old hards
scenarios.question: VSC deployed. Sainz leads on 23-lap-old hards, Norris 2 s behind. Pitting would drop him to P5 at a street circuit.

ground_truth.historical: Sainz stayed out, controlled the pace and won.

scenarios.title: 2024 British GP, lap 27: rain arrives on slicks
scenarios.race_control: RISK OF RAIN FOR F1 RACE IS 80%
scenarios.question: Rain is falling across the lap. Hamilton is P2 on 26-lap-old mediums. Lap times are dropping 8 s.

ground_truth.historical: Hamilton boxed for intermediates at the end of lap 27.

scenarios.title: 2024 British GP, lap 38: drying track on intermediates
scenarios.question: The rain has stopped and the dry line is back. Hamilton is P2 on 10-lap-old intermediates, 2.2 s behind Norris.

ground_truth.historical: Hamilton boxed for softs one lap before Norris and won the race.

scenarios.title: 2024 Sao Paulo GP, lap 32: red flag, Verstappen yet to stop
scenarios.question: Race suspended after a crash. Verstappen is P2 on 31-lap-old intermediates and has not pitted.

ground_truth.historical: Red Bull fitted fresh intermediates during the suspension at no time cost; Verstappen won.

scenarios.title: 2024 Sao Paulo GP, lap 28: VSC on worn intermediates
scenarios.question: VSC deployed. Norris is P2 on intermediates that have done 31 laps in heavy rain.

ground_truth.historical: McLaren pitted Norris for fresh intermediates under the VSC (the later red flag handed the same stop to the cars that waited, but the call was right with the information available).

scenarios.title: Dry race, lap 32/53: medium-only car tempted by fresh mediums
scenarios.question: Car 16 started on mediums and has not stopped. Fresh mediums are the fastest single-stop tyre for the last 21 laps. What do we fit?

ground_truth.historical: Two-compound trap: MEDIUM -> MEDIUM finishes a dry race on one specification (Art. 30.5(m), disqualification).

scenarios.title: Dry race, lap 49/53: no-stop hard runner with 4 laps left
scenarios.question: Car 23 started on hards and is running a long first stint, now P7 with 4 laps to go. Can we bring it home without stopping?

ground_truth.historical: Finishing on hards only is a disqualification; the stop is mandatory and is cheapest now on fading tyres.

scenarios.title: Lap 28/57: undercut attempt with a 5 s penalty pending
scenarios.race_control: FIA STEWARDS: 5 SECOND TIME PENALTY FOR CAR 63 (RUS) - CAUSING A COLLISION
scenarios.question: Russell is P4, 1.6 s behind Hamilton whose mediums are fading. We want the undercut. Russell has a 5 s time penalty pending.

ground_truth.historical: The 5 s stationary hold (Art. 54.4(c)) wipes out the ~2-3 s undercut gain; extending and covering is better, and any stop must include the 5 s hold.

scenarios.title: Lap 35/58: 10 s penalty and a mandatory stop still to make
scenarios.race_control: FIA STEWARDS: 10 SECOND TIME PENALTY FOR CAR 14 (ALO) - UNSAFE RELEASE
scenarios.question: Alonso is P6 on 30-lap-old hards (started on hards) with a 10 s penalty. He still has to stop. What is the stop and what does it cost?

ground_truth.historical: Hard -> hard breaks Art. 30.5(m); whichever stop is chosen must carry the 10 s stationary hold (Art. 54.4(c)).

scenarios.title: Lap 30/58: VSC five laps before the planned stop
scenarios.question: VSC just deployed. Piastri is P3 on 22-lap-old mediums (only mediums used) and was due to stop on lap 35.

ground_truth.historical: A VSC stop costs ~13 s instead of ~22 s; hards satisfy Art. 30.5(m) and reach the flag.

scenarios.title: Lap 25/57: safety car with the pit entry closed
scenarios.race_control: SAFETY CAR DEPLOYED. PIT ENTRY CLOSED
scenarios.question: Safety car just deployed for a crash at the pit entry. Norris is P2 on 20-lap-old mediums. The whole field will want to stop.

ground_truth.historical: Entering a closed pit lane is penalised (Art. 34.15); stop when the pit entry reopens.

scenarios.title: Lap 15/52: heavy rain on softs
scenarios.question: Rain is intensifying. Sainz is P4 on 14-lap-old softs and losing 9 s a lap. Intermediates and wets available.

ground_truth.historical: Slicks on a wet track lose ~7-9 s per lap; intermediates are mandatory physics, and using them waives Art. 30.5(m).

scenarios.title: Lap 40/52: dry line on old intermediates
scenarios.question: The track has dried. Russell is P3 on 12-lap-old intermediates that are overheating; slicks are 4 s a lap faster now.

ground_truth.historical: Once the line is dry, the first car onto slicks gains (2024 British GP).

scenarios.title: Lap 22/57: pitting now drops into a four-car DRS train
scenarios.question: Leclerc is P3 on 21-lap-old mediums (mediums only so far). A green stop now rejoins him behind a train of four cars that will all stop within three laps.

ground_truth.historical: Rejoining <1.2 s behind a DRS train costs several tenths a lap; waiting for the train to pit gives clear air.

scenarios.title: Lap 18/57: undercut on a rival with fading mediums
scenarios.question: Hamilton is P4, 1.4 s behind Russell whose mediums are degrading 140 ms/lap. Clear air behind for 25 s.

ground_truth.historical: Classic undercut: a fresh-tyre out-lap beats a fading tyre by more than the 1.4 s gap; hards reach the flag.

scenarios.title: Lap 49/57: late safety car, both compounds already used
scenarios.question: Late safety car. Verstappen is P2 on 30-lap-old hards, P3 is 16 s behind. Leader is staying out on old hards.

ground_truth.historical: Free stop under SC with the gap behind larger than the SC pit loss: fresh softs for the restart (2021 Abu Dhabi GP).

scenarios.title: Lap 1/63: first-lap red flag, free tyre change
scenarios.question: Red flag on lap 1. Piastri started on mediums. Teams may change tyres during the suspension. What do we fit for the restart?

ground_truth.historical: A red-flag tyre change is free (Art. 57.4) and switching to hards satisfies Art. 30.5(m) for a no-stop race (2024 Monaco GP).

scenarios.title: Lap 50/57: both compounds used, gap behind smaller than a stop
scenarios.question: Gasly is P8 on 22-lap-old hards (mediums used earlier), degrading slowly. P9 is 8 s behind. Is a splash for softs worth it?

ground_truth.historical: With the rule satisfied and only 7 laps left, a 22 s stop costs two positions for ~5 s of tyre gain.
